passages.original: 45 X. Quod gratia Dei non solum peccata demittat, sed etiam adjuvet ne committantur, et praestat ut lex impleatur, non, sicut ait Pelagius, facile, quasi sine gratia Dei difficilius poscit impleri.
passages.english: 45 X. That the grace of God not only forgives sins but also helps [us] so that they are not committed, and grants that the law be fulfilled, not, as Pelagius says, [more] easily, as if without the grace of God it could be fulfilled [only] with greater difficulty.
passages.notes: This is a chapter heading, probably the tenth canon on grace of the Council of Carthage (418), as transmitted in the Pseudo-Isidorian collection. The printed 'poscit' is very likely an error for 'possit' ('could'), and is translated so. 'demittat' stands for 'dimittat' ('forgives'). The construction 'non ... facile' is compressed; it is taken to mean that grace does not merely make fulfilment of the law easier.

passages.original: III. Ut Irenaeus remotus a Barcinonensi ad propriam reverteretur. (??)
passages.english: III. That Irenaeus, removed from [the see of] Barcelona, should return to his own [church].
passages.notes: A chapter heading. The "(??)" stands in the source text and has not been translated. "Barcinonensi" is an adjective whose noun is not expressed; "see" or "church" is understood, and "propriam" ("his own") likewise implies "church".

passages.original: Item Chronica Eusebii Caesariensis, atque ejusdem historiae ecclesiasticae libros, quamvis in primo nar- rationis suae libro tepuerit, et post in laudibus at- que excusatione Origenis schismatici unum con- scripserit librum; propter rerum tamen singularium notitiam, quae ad instructionem pertinent, usque- quaque non dicimus renuendos.
passages.english: Likewise the Chronicle of Eusebius of Caesarea, and the books of his Ecclesiastical History: although he grew lukewarm in the first book of his narrative, and afterwards wrote a book in praise and defence of Origen the schismatic, nevertheless, because of [their] knowledge of particular matters that serve for instruction, we do not say that they are to be rejected altogether.
passages.notes: Line-break hyphenations in the source ("nar- rationis", "at- que", "con- scripserit", "usque- quaque") have been read as single words. "Tepuerit" ("grew lukewarm") presumably refers to doctrinal tepidity.
